name: Cotinga Purple
lede: Cotinga Purple is a dark reddish purple named for the cotinga, a family of brightly colored tropical birds, recorded in Ridgway's 1912 standard.

sections.title: Named for a tropical bird
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* lists Cotinga Purple on plate XI, hue 63, tone k [1]. Maerz and Paul repeat the name in 1930, on their plate 45 L 10, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 assigns it block 219, deep purple, 5.1 units from that block's centroid [2]. The nearest other named color in our library is [[byzantium]], 5.2 units away [2].

Cotingas are a family of South and Central American birds, and several species, among them the purple-breasted cotinga, show the dark, slightly red-leaning purple this name describes; Ridgway drew on ornithology, not botany, for this plate [1]. It sits among the dark reddish purples near [[plum]] and [[mulberry]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Cotinga Purple covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 2 of them, as photographed [3]. Both uses are as a shadow rather than a highlight, fitting a color this dark [3]. The earliest is an 1890 Indian painting, *Dusmanta Garlanding Shakumtala* [3]. A color this dark and specific rarely covers enough of an aged, varnished canvas to be detected at our threshold, which is why so few paintings register it [3].
